title: Suppressing FileDropzone's built-in caption and testing it
answers: How to hide FileDropzone's 'Accepted file types' text
FileDropzone tests fail with getByText not finding dropzone text
body:
Symptom: FileDropzone always renders its own 'Accepted file types: ...' caption and there is no prop to disable it, causing duplicate/unwanted text when the accepted types are already shown elsewhere (e.g. in a Field description).
Fix pattern: wrap the FileDropzone in a container styled with `small { display: none }` (emotion css) to hide the built-in caption, and put the accepted-types text in the surrounding `Field`'s `description` prop instead — see `hideAcceptedFileTypesCaption` in public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/steps/Step1AlertmanagerResources.tsx.
Constraint/invariant: FileDropzone is lazy-loaded via React.lazy/Suspense, so tests must use `findByText`/`await` (not synchronous `getByText`) to see its content, and real drag-and-drop bypasses the OS file-dialog `accept` filter that `userEvent.upload` normally simulates — use `userEvent.setup({ applyAccept: false })` when testing rejection of disallowed file types, per public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/steps/Step1AlertmanagerResources.test.tsx.
applies: Any component or test that uses Grafana's FileDropzone
says: File upload shows duplicate accepted file types text
Hide the built-in file type caption in upload
Remove automatic file types message from dropzone
Suppress file upload component default accepted types text
File upload caption overlaps with form field description
search: Hiding FileDropzone's built-in accepted-types caption requires wrapping it in a container with `small { display: none }` CSS and placing the text in the surrounding Field's description prop instead. FileDropzone is lazy-loaded via React.lazy/Suspense, so tests must use `findByText`/`await` instead of synchronous `getByText` to access its rendered content. Real drag-and-drop interactions bypass the OS file-dialog `accept` filter that `userEvent.upload` normally simulates, so use `userEvent.setup({ applyAccept: false })` when testing rejection of disallowed file types. See `hideAcceptedFileTypesCaption` in Step1AlertmanagerResources.tsx and its test file for the implementation pattern. This guidance applies to any component or test code that uses Grafana's FileDropzone.
